subject: Data routing & lawful transfer Q&A — Bioreach RFP appendix
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@bioreach.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco D'Angelo <m.dangelo@bioreach.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarification on routing and lawful transfers for RFP appendix

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the RFP appendix — quick follow-ups from our privacy/legal team on cross-border handling before we finalise scoring:

1) Can you confirm the default geographic residency of inference workloads for EU customers and whether customers can pin region per-tenant?
2) Which transfer mechanisms do you rely on for EU->US model calls (SCCs, DPF, other)? Do you publish executed SCC templates or is that handled per-contract?
3) Where are logs (request/response, audit) stored and who has access? Retention defaults and options?
4) We need a short list of subprocessors that could access personal data during inference (model hosting, telemetry, monitoring, logging).

Can you provide concise answers we can include in the procurement appendix? If you have a diagram that maps request routing (ingress -> model -> logs -> storage) that would be great.

Best,
Elena
Legal Operations — Bioreach Therapeutics

---

Note: this is part of the Bioreach RFP (section 7.4).
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@bioreach.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-24T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on routing and lawful transfers for RFP appendix

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I attached a simple datapath diagram. Monica (ops) and Karthik (legal) are cc'd for technical/contract-level follow-ups.

1) Residency and regional pinning
- Default hosted deployment: workload region follows customer account region. For EU customers we default to EU regions (Frankfurt or Paris) unless customer elects otherwise.
- Yes — customers can pin per-tenant/namespace to an explicit region or set routing policies. Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments allow full customer-controlled residency.

2) Transfer mechanisms
- We support multiple mechanisms: EU Model hosting in-region (preferred), Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs, DPF, other)?
- Executed SCC templates: we provide our standard SCC annex in the contract paperwork; final executed copies are included with enterprise deals. For procurement scoring you can reference: "Redwood provides SCCs and a documented DPF assessment; executed SCCs are supplied on contract execution."

3) Logs — storage and access
- Request/response transient logs: by default we redact full response bodies in long-term logs; request metadata and token-level telemetry are retained for 30 days. Audit logs (control-plane events, role changes) are retained for 365 days by default.
- Access: customer admins (if in Dedicated/Private) and a limited ops on-call group (hosted support) with role-based access. Customers can request extended retention or alternative retention/archival in contract.

4) Subprocessors
- Short list: cloud infra provider (GCP/AWS region-specific), managed logging vendor (LogStream Inc.), model optimization partner (QuantOpt Labs), telemetry/metric provider (PulseMetrics). We provide a complete subprocessor list on request and publish updates in our transparency portal.

Next steps: Monica and Karthik will prepare a concise appendix answer and flag any items that require contract-level language.

Best,
Sean
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-datapaths-diagram.pdf (pdf)

Date: 2026-08-30T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: need clarity on telemetry and redaction controls

Monica/Sean — quick question from our privacy engineering team: you mentioned request metadata and token-level telemetry are retained for 30 days. We need to know:

A) Are response bodies ever stored in full in logs for hosted accounts? If so, under what conditions (debug mode, support request)?
B) Can customers toggle redaction to ensure no PII leaves customer-controlled storage?

This will determine whether we classify the product as "processor with potential access to content" vs "processor with no content retention."

Thanks,
Marco
Privacy Engineer — Bioreach
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Marco D'Angelo <m.dangelo@bioreach.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@bioreach.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-02T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: need clarity on telemetry and redaction controls

Marco — good questions; below is the concise, procurement-friendly language you can include in the RFP appendix. Monica/Karthik: please flag if we need tighter legal wording.

A) Response bodies and debug retention
- By default, Redwood hosted accounts do NOT persist full response bodies in long-term logs. We collect minimal request metadata and token-level telemetry for performance/quality monitoring.
- Full response bodies are only captured in the following scenarios: (1) customer enables "support/debug" capture explicitly for a session and authorises capture via the Console, or (2) customer submits interaction transcripts to Support (redwood-support@redwood.ai) for troubleshooting. Such captures are time-limited and accessible only to authorised support and the requesting customer.

B) Redaction controls and customer toggles
- Customers can enable strict redaction at the account level: when enabled, response payloads are stripped of any detected PII before any telemetry export or long-term logging. This is available in Hosted and Dedicated. Private deployments offer full control — logs remain in customer-managed storage.

Procurement-ready summary (one paragraph)
- "Redwood defaults to EU-hosted runtime for EU accounts and supports per-tenant regional pinning. Data transfers are managed via in-region hosting, SCCs, and documented DPF assessments. By default Redwood does not retain full response bodies; customers can enable session capture for support or opt-in to debug captures. Account-level redaction is available and Private deployments keep all logs in customer-managed storage. A current subprocessor list and sample SCC are available on request."

Next steps: I'll attach the sample SCC and the subprocessor CSV to this thread for Bioreach procurement. Can we schedule a 30-minute call next week to walk legal/engineering through the diagram and any contract clauses?

Thanks,
Sean
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments: sample-sccs-executed.pdf (pdf), processor-declaration-20260901.csv (csv)
